Tissue Culture Dry Run Assignment

Tissue Culture Dry Run Assignment

You will make a batch of media with our lab protocol, then run four cultures that change only the auxin and cytokinin. You will watch each explant grow for four weeks and compare what it makes: roots, shoots, or callus.

What you will do

  1. Media prep room: follow our Media Preparation protocol to make 1 liter of media.
  2. Four runs: set NAA and BAP, place the explant in the hood, grow it.
  3. Compare your four runs on a table and chart.
  4. Answer 12 questions, then export your PDF.

Finish in one sitting. If you reload the page, you start over.

Media prep room

Part 1: Make 1 liter of media

Follow our Media Preparation protocol in order. Use the houseplant rows on the Media Material Measurements chart. Your explant is a houseplant leaf.

Step 1: Sterilize the containers

The growing containers go in the Steroclave while you make the media.

Steps 2 to 7: Mix

Stir bar on. Add each one in this order.

Gamborg vitamins
 

Step 8: Heat-stable PGRs only

Which PGRs can go in now, before the Steroclave? Heat-sensitive ones wait until step 18: filter-sterilize and add them in the hood once the media cools to 140 °F. You will pick your NAA and BAP amounts for each run in Part 2.

Steps 9 and 10: Bring it to volume

Step 11: Adjust the pH to 5.8

Add single drops of 1M NaOH and watch the meter. One drop at a time so you do not go past 5.8.

    Every media type: sucrose 30 g, PPM 1 mL, pH 5.8 adjusted with 1M NaOH. Use agar or gellan gum, not both. PGR stocks are 1 mg/mL, so 1 mL = 1 mg/L. Heat stable (add at step 8, before the Steroclave): IBA, NAA, BAP, TDZ. Heat sensitive (filter-sterilize, add in the hood after the media cools to 140 °F): GA3, IAA.
